texts.label: text
texts.orig: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) is a cutting-edge metal additive manufacturing technology that enables the precise construction of complex geometries layer by layer. It is widely used in aerospace, medical, and automotive industries due to its unmatched design flexibility. However, LPBF faces several challenges: Process variations lead to defects that affect mechanical properties. Traditional defect detection methods, such as X-ray computed tomography, are slow and costly. It also has a limitation on specimen size. Real-time monitoring is limited without labeled data, making it difficult to detect quality issues during printing rather than after fabrication.

texts.label: text
texts.orig:
Key defects include keyhole, porosity, surface roughness, and distortion.
Keyhole formation, which happens when excessive laser energy causes deep vapor cavities, weakening the structure. Porosity, which occurs when the melt pool is too shallow and insufficiently fused. Surface roughness and distortion, which degrade mechanical properties and often require post-processing.

texts.label: text
texts.orig:
Another challenge in LPBF is to get smooth surface roughness. melt pool stability and spatter control are key factors in achieving a smooth surface finish. Instabilities in the melt pool lead to excessive spatter, which in turn increases surface roughness and defects in the final part. Generally, Melt pool stability impacts the global surface roughness, since it dictates the overall uniformity of the layer deposition and the formation of defect. Spatter influences the local surface roughness – as individual spatter particles settle on specific areas, creating localized surface irregularities and defects.
Proper laser parameter tuning, powder bed cleanliness, and optimized gas flow can mitigate these issues, leading to better surface quality and mechanical performance of printed components.

Six key metrics were computed, which are melt pool intensity and area, plume intensity and area, and spatter intensity and area.
